newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cut-value S&P 500 LEAPS a focus.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cut-value S&P 500 LEAPS a focus.

text.p: Reduced-value LEAPS (Long Term Equity Anticipation Securities) on the S&P 500 index grabbed the spotlight in an otherwise sluggish trading day, traders said Thursday.
Nearly 32,000 of the reduced value S&P 500 index put options with an expiration in December 1998 .LSY traded at the 80 strike price and 30,860 of the LSY 65 puts traded.
The index is one-tenth the value of the S&P 500 .SPX and was down 0.62 at 79.95 in afternoon trading.
The S&P 500 was off 6.23 at 799.45.
Harrison Roth, senior options strategist at Cowen & Co, said it appeared the LEAPS investor bought the 80-strike puts and sold the 65-strike ones.
"It's a new trade on both sides," he said. "Buying the 80 put and selling the 65 put to reduce cost."
Big trades were also seen in the reduced-value S&P 500 index LEAPS that have expirations in December 1999 .LSX.
The LSX 80 put traded about 10,100 contracts, the 100 call traded 3,000, the 75 put traded 1,750 and the 77-1/2 put traded 1,600.
Roth said it was difficult to determine what those investors were doing.
The LSX 80 put had open interest of 6,382 through Wednesday and the 100 call was added today so had no contracts open.
Roth noted that while the 100 strike was added in the LSX options, the 1,000 strike was not added in the S&P 500 LEAPS that have expirations in June and December 1998 .SPL.
A trader in S&P 500 options at the CBOE said the volume numbers on those reduced-value LEAPS were a little misleading since the index was only one-tenth the size of the S&P 500.
The 30,000 contracts traded in the LSY, for instance, would be 3,000 contracts in the SPX.
But still the volume was respectable given the tepid trade that has hit the larger S&P 500, traders said.
"It's been very, very slow," the S&P 500 options trader said. "Everyone's sitting around."
Among the few highlights, one institution sold 2,000 June 850 calls and another institution was selling May 810 calls.
In the March series, the most action was in the 780, where 5,375 contracts changed hands, and the 820 call, where about 5,200 changed hands.
Overall, SPX put volume at the CBOE outpaced call volume by 35,565 to 12,826 by 1400 CST/2000 GMT.
In other major index options trading, put volume in the S&P 100 index .OEX topped call volume by 42,805 to 30,071.
The only OEX call trading more than 4,000 contracts was the March 800, with volume of about 4,160.
The March 745 put traded about 7,065 and the March 780 put traded 6,400, making them the most active OEX puts.
The underlying index was down 8.42 at 776.17.
